# Pinned Ensemble core for LIFE030

This product includes software developed by the University of California,
Santa Cruz and its contributors.

Source: [ensemble-engine/ensemble](https://github.com/ensemble-engine/ensemble/tree/8b74bdec4ba2ef4e14795b7591df3b5d73f283e3),
revision `8b74bdec4ba2ef4e14795b7591df3b5d73f283e3`. The original
[BSD-4-Clause license](LICENSE.md) is retained verbatim. Root distribution notices
are maintained by the application packaging owner.

`upstream/*.js.txt` are the seven original standalone modules in their original
build order. The `.txt` suffix keeps formatters from changing upstream bytes.
`manifest.json` records each original path/hash, ordered exact source patches,
and the resulting patched hash. The runtime loader checks both hashes and each
unique patch anchor before assembling a private instance. No authored text is
compiled as source. The research checkout is never needed at runtime.

`underscore.ts` is an independently written four-function compatibility subset
(keys, size, stable sortBy and inclusive random), under Lina's Apache-2.0 license.
It is not copied from Underscore. The pinned original Underscore and Lovers and
Rivals fixtures are retained only under the runtime test tree for comparative
behavior checks; neither ships in this production subtree.

Local patches expose complete mutable state and immutable definition inventories;
select the exact requested root through the original hierarchy with explicit
acceptance; remove the implicit negative-volition refusal only on that explicit
path; support either-response terminals; constrain concrete/role bindings;
bound queries, writes and recursive binding work; record matched triggers; and
clamp historical lookup windows at introduction boundaries. The numeric influence
maximum starts at negative infinity rather than an undocumented willingness floor.
A reciprocal write searches with its identity pattern, preventing effect operators
from creating duplicate reverse facts. An empty authored schema is allowed for a
rootless move/goal/reveal capability. Each change appears separately in the manifest.

Trace capacity never truncates the action search. Every eligible DAG path remains
available with its original weights and bindings, while the consumer receives
each terminal candidate ID once. If that complete ID list exceeds the trace
budget, the proposal fails before random selection or result production. Historical
queries also respect the bootstrap introduction boundary at social step zero.

The host retains all history fields and property order, offstage/eliminated lists,
iterator/no-repeat counters, volition cache/cursors, variables and introduction
metadata, and versioned LCG state/draw count. Three upstream accidental globals are
localized to each assembled instance; they are transient evaluation scratch.
Immutable tables are rebuilt from typed compiler data and checked for mutation.

One owned Linux process executes each proposal under DATA 512 MiB, CPU 3 seconds,
zero core/file-size limits, a separate empty working directory, minimal environment,
no env-file loading and no package auto-install. Wall time and pipes are bounded;
abort/failure returns only after child exit. This is a validated-data application
boundary, not a hostile-host, filesystem, or network sandbox. Missing `prlimit`
support fails closed. Only the main service can accept receipts or change storage.
